title: Tenant-affinity mismatch for API keys causing intermittent cross-org access
creator: Maya Chen
description: Several enterprise customers reported seeing resources (routes, jobs, and model audit traces) from other organizations in their consoles after a sequence of API key rotations and edge-caching events. This affects Hosted and Dedicated customers, and we've reproduced the same behavior on a Private deployment configuration with shared proxy templates. The issue manifests as authorization scoping being bypassed for a small fraction of requests during token refresh and API key rotation windows.
symptoms_and_scope: Intermittent cross-org visibility and occasional unauthorized API responses were observed between 2025-11-03 22:40 UTC and 2025-11-04 03:20 UTC. Affected surfaces: management console, /v1/keys endpoints, and real-time logs. Approximately 6 customers confirmed exposure; estimated request leakage window per-customer averaged 2-7 minutes during maintenance rolls.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use API key A (org-A) to start a long-lived websocket/stream against /v1/streams
2) Trigger an API key rotation for org-A while simultaneous rotation happens for org-B in the same region and proxy pool

3) Observe that cached auth context for a small number of connections is replaced with the wrong org id after proxied token refresh; subsequent requests carry org-B scope but remain attributed to API key A
4) Reproduce locally by running a proxy pool with short TTL cache and concurrent key-rotation scripts for two orgs (scripts attached in investigation notes)
alternatively, reproduce on dedicated by running a canary rotation across two nodes sharing a KV prefix
Note: reproduction is timing-dependent; increase throughput and shorten cache TTL to reliably trigger the window
investigation_notes: Initial logs show a race in auth context refresh: when token refresh logic writes a new tenant mapping into the shared proxy-level cache (redis key prefix 'auth:tenant'), a stale mapping can be re-used by an unrelated connection that has an in-memory pointer to the same cache slot. The root cause is twofold: 1) re-use of a non-tenant-isolated cache key namespace in the edge proxy, and 2) a code path that silently promotes a refreshed mapping into per-connection context without validating the derived org id against the presenting API key. We also found a batching optimization in the token refresh worker that merges refreshes across API keys for the same proxy shard; merging logic did not include tenant-level guards.
logs_summary: Spans and traces show auth-refresh events where cache_set(key=auth:tenant:shard-12) occurs with org_id=org-B while a connection previously tagged org-A reads auth:get(shard-12) immediately afterwards. Correlation IDs and timestamps attached in related_prs. No database corruption detected.
root_cause: Shared proxy cache key namespace combined with a refresh-merge optimization allowed tenant mappings from one rotation to be applied to concurrent connections for a different API key. The connection-level update lacked an assertion that the new tenant id matches the API key's expected org, allowing a short window of cross-org authorization.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Disable refresh-merge optimization in edge proxy (hotfix deployed to region-us-east-1 at 2025-11-04 01:05 UTC). 2) Set cache TTL to 0 for auth:tenant keys for the most active shards to prevent reuse while we patch. 3) Notify affected customers and rotate server-side audit tokens. Hotfix removed the majority of leakage within 20 minutes.
remediation_plan: A. Patch edge proxy to namespace auth cache keys by API key fingerprint and region (auth:tenant:<shard>:<key-fingerprint>) and add a defensive check that rejects a candidate tenant mapping if it doesn't match the presenting API key's expected org.
B. Add unit + integration tests that simulate concurrent rotations and verify there is no cross-org mapping in the cache, include a timing-fuzz harness.
C. Expand tracing to include expected_org_id in auth-refresh spans and add an alert when candidate_org != expected_org for any refresh event.
D. Backfill a migration job to rekey existing auth:tenant keys with the new namespace and validate shard consistency.
E. Update Dedicated/Private deployment ops runbook to ensure proxy config uses per-tenant cache namespaces and to document steps for safe rotations.
F. Schedule an audit and customer outreach follow-up with legal and security for confirmed exposures.
rollback_plan: If the namespaced-key patch causes regressions, rollback by reverting the proxy binary and re-applying the temporary TTL and disabled-merge config; ensure we maintain the increased tracing and customer notifications during rollback.
testing_plan: Run canary in staging with high concurrency and accelerated TTLs for 48 hours. Create synthetic clients that run concurrent rotation scenarios and assert 0 cross-org responses. Run Dedicated and Private deployment smoke tests with default proxy template and with on-prem template variations.
deployment_plan: 1) Merge PR and run CI with new tests. 2) Deploy to canary shard (shard-12) in us-east-1 for 2h. 3) If green, roll sequentially across proxy shards with automated health checks for auth mismatch alerts. 4) After full roll, increase monitoring retention for auth-refresh spans for 72h.
